newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani authority seeks broker default details.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani authority seeks broker default details.

text.p: Pakistan's Corporate Law Authority (CLA) has asked the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) to provide details of transactions by defaulting broker M. Rashid Jamal, a CLA official said on Friday.
He said the CLA had written to the KSE on Thursday asking it for details of deals in which Jamal's MRJ Securities had sold shares short or bought shares but did not collect them.
The CLA also asked the KSE for a breakdown of all claims by investors, excluding KSE members, against Jamal and how the bourse proposed to settle them.

The official, who asked not to be named, said the authority wanted to know how much the KSE had raised by selling Jamal's membership card and whether any of the proceeds had been used to reimburse investors or whether only brokers had benefited.
The KSE removed Jamal's seat at the bourse last week, saying his company had failed to pay money owed in share transactions and to deliver sold shares on settlement day.
The KSE is reported to have auctioned Jamal's trading card and other assets at the bourse to raise money to settle claims.

The KSE, which has a clearing house protection fund with a limit of 12.5 million rupees to bridge any shortfall in meeting the registered claims of a defaulting member, says claims of 60 million rupees ($1.45 million) against the firm are covered.
The CLA official said it was not yet clear how much Jamal owed, adding that it could be as much as 250 million rupees.
Stocks analysts say the CLA is keen to crack down on underlying regulatory problems at the Karachi Stock Exchange.
On Wednesday the CLA barred stock broker Zafar Moti from the Karachi and Lahore bourses for alleged trading law violations. ($1 = 41.5 rupees)
